correctness.rationale: For an interior point of an m-dimensional Euclidean ball, the positive radial root is explicit. Spherical integration cancels its odd linear term, and the remaining square-root integrand is strictly decreasing in eccentricity away from the polar set; for m>=2 this gives strict monotonicity of the whole integral. An affine hyperplane section of an ambient ball is centered at the projection of the ambient center, and the section-center distance squared is the ambient norm squared minus one H-dependent constant. Hence every section comparison and the full comparison are equivalent to the same norm ordering. The packaged checker reconstructs the algebra and the m=1 boundary phenomenon.

value.rationale: The claim is a natural exact model case of a published convex-geometric implication, not an arbitrary ball integral. It sharpens the open problem's hypothesis from all common hyperplanes to any single common hyperplane and explains this by a dimension-free eccentricity-order mechanism. The precise failure at ambient dimension two also isolates the role of section dimension.
